# Logic

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
`ui` (**U**ser **I**nterface)

The container, whatever sees the user

Used for setting the desired configurations of options that will be elaborated in the server

Used for displaying the results of the computations that took place in the server
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
`server`

It gets the work done, according to the configuration set in the UI

Replaces the results into the allocated spaces
:::

:::

UI and Server work in a flow, communicating to each other (@fig-uiServer).

::: {#fig-uiServer layout-ncol=1}

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

    UI["**UI**<br/><br/>Set the options<br/>Displays the results"]
    SERVER["**SERVER**<br/><br/>Elaborates the options<br/>Sends back the results"]

    UI -->|"Input"| SERVER
    SERVER -->|"Output"| UI

    style UI fill:#2b6c8e,stroke:#1b4258,stroke-width:2px,color:#ffffff
    style SERVER fill:#8fd36f,stroke:#4c8b3a,stroke-width:2px,color:#ffffff

    linkStyle default stroke:#FFD700,stroke-width:5px
```

Interaction between the user interface (UI) and the server.

:::

# Basics

```r
install.packages("shiny") # install
library(shiny) # use it
```

```r
ui = fluidPage(          # <1>
   [...]                 # <1>
  )                      # <1>
server = function(input, output){ # <2>
  [...]                           # <2>
}                                 # <2>
shinyApp(ui, server)  # <3>
```

1. Define the ui
2. Define the server
3. Shine

The `ui` contains two kinds of elements:

- **inputs**, the controls the user plays with (a menu, a slider, a box to type in, a button…)
- **outputs**, empty boxes where the server will put the results (a text, a plot, a table…)

There is a widget for (almost) everything: numbers, text, dates, files… We see the most useful ones in [Input widgets](03-inputs.qmd) and [Outputs and render functions](04-outputs.qmd).

# A first app

[Input]{.io-chip .io-chip-in} and [output]{.io-chip .io-chip-out}, in the `ui` and in the `server`:

::: {.io-first-app}
```r
ui = fluidPage(
  selectInput(inputId = "mySelection",
              label = h3("Select box"),
              choices = list("Choice 1" = 1, "Choice 2" = 2, "Choice 3" = 3),
              selected = 1),
  verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "myOutput")
)

server = function(input, output) {
  output$myOutput = renderPrint({
    paste("This is my choice:", input$mySelection)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
:::

- In the `ui`, `selectInput()` creates a menu called `mySelection`, and `verbatimTextOutput()` reserves an empty box called `myOutput`
- In the `server`, `input$mySelection` reads the choice of the user, and `output$myOutput` fills the box with the result

The names are what connects the two pieces: we look at them closely in [How Shiny thinks](02-logic.qmd).

## An astonishing result

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [viewer]
#| viewerHeight: 220
library(shiny)

ui = fluidPage(
  selectInput(inputId = "mySelection",
              label = h3("Select box"),
              choices = list("Choice 1" = 1, "Choice 2" = 2, "Choice 3" = 3),
              selected = 1),
  verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "myOutput")
)

server = function(input, output) {
  output$myOutput = renderPrint({
    paste("This is my choice:", input$mySelection)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

In the next page we put this same app in an RStudio project, with the `ui` in a script called `ui.R` and the `server` in a script called `server.R`.
